Seminar Title:

3D Progressive Damage Analysis of GFRP Laminate in a Single Lap Joint: An Integrated Experimental, Numerical and Machine Learning Approach

Seminar Type:

Department:

Speaker Name:

Deepti Ranjan Mohapatra ( Rollno : 521ce6017)

Speaker Type:

Venue:

Seminar Room Civil Engineering Department

14 Aug 2026 05:00 PM

Contact:

Subhajit Mondal

Abstract:

In this study, the mechanical response of a woven Glass Fibre Reinforced Polymer (GFRP) in a Single Lap Bolted Joint (SLBJ) configuration is analysed for uncertainties associated with geometrical parameters, including the ratios of edge distance to bolt diameter (e1/db), laminate width to bolt diameter (w/db) and laminate length to bolt diameter (L/db), bolt diameter to plate thickness (db/tp), and bolt-hole clearance (cl). The experimentally obtained responses are validated using a Finite Element (FE) model incorporating a 3D Progressive Damage Model (PDM). The failure criteria are modified for woven GFRP and implemented using a user material subroutine, UMAT. A peak load deviation of 2.13% between experimental investigations and the FE model suggests the effectiveness of the 3D model. A sampling method is proposed in this study that significantly reduces the required dataset size to accurately represent the entire design space, resulting from parametric variation in the case of the SLBJ. The effectiveness of the sampling technique is further verified with a 2D scatterplot matrix. The bootstrap Root Mean Square Error (RMSE), with a 95% confidence interval ranging from 0.330 to 0.659, and the bootstrap R2 distribution, with a 95% confidence interval between 0.965 and 0.992, suggest stable and reliable sampling. Furthermore, an L2 discrepancy of 1.48% between the proposed sampling and the benchmarked Latin Hypercube Sampling (LHS) provides the final quantitative assessment. A robust ML meta-model, adaptive in handling noise in the dataset, has been developed by using an ensemble method. This model effectively maps the underlying correlation among the feature parameters. The developed meta-model, with an R2 value of 0.99, is used as a surrogate model for Global Sensitivity Analysis (GSA) using the first and total order Sobol index. A design space is developed using the Central Composite Design (CCD) of Response Surface Methodology (RSM) to statistically designate critical points and significantly reduce the required dataset for variation analysis. The optimised geometrical parameters are observed to maximise the peak load by 75.39% in comparison to the baseline model. Furthermore, the bond strength capability of epoxy-based adhesive used for woven-type GFRP in a Single Lap Adhesive Joint (SLAJ) configuration. 3D Cohesive Zone Modelling (CZM) is utilised to simulate the failure behaviour in the adhesive layer. A design space is constructed using CCD to acquire unique parametric combinations which retain most of the variability in the design space. The viability of this model is further verified by using a hybrid Adaptive Neuro-Fuzzy Inference System (ANFIS). The investigation is concluded with a

sensitivity analysis using SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), suggesting width to be the most sensitive parameter for peak load variation. Furthermore, a comparative analysis on the responses of all the considered joint configurations is performed to have deep insight into the joint behaviour upon variation in the geometrical parameters, which is crucial from the design point of view.
